A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–L. Matching content across appendix repagination supports a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v6 reports original sequential-pricing simulations in Section 6 and Appendix J, measuring estimation errors, Nash-equilibrium convergence, and regret, including robustness experiments.

after.justification: v7 retains these original simulations and their results in Section 6, Appendix J, and Figures 5–8.

M1.justification: SPE-BR in Algorithm 1 is unchanged: separate estimation of the parametric component and s-concave demand link, followed by estimated best-response pricing. No algorithmic component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic pricing markets with 2, 4, and 6 sellers and Gaussian-CDF demand links. Coverage of unequal exploration lengths and shape-parameter misspecification is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate Algorithm 1 across parameter regimes without an empirical comparison against another pricing algorithm. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix J retain the same price domain, demand noise, horizons, exploration procedures, parameter settings, and evaluation metrics. Expanded contents entries do not introduce new experiments or protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix J.1–J.3 retains the same contraction-constant sensitivity, unequal-exploration, and shape-misspecification analyses, with unchanged evidence in Figures 5–8.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 independent simulation repetitions, averages, and 95% confidence intervals. Run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The aligned result panels in Figures 5–8 are identical, including plotted outcomes, fitted slopes, and uncertainty bands. Their accompanying numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorems, derivations, and appendix proofs are retained. Appendix L corrects u_i to u_1 in an existing scaling argument; this is an index typo correction, without a substantive change to the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same semiparametric pricing proposal, equilibrium guarantees, regret bounds, and concentration results. No principal claim is added, strengthened, or narrowed.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning common exploration, known shape parameters, misspecification robustness, and algorithmic collusion are unchanged. Appendix L's copyediting preserves its existing explanation.

D1.justification: Implementation and simulation details in Appendices A, D, and J are unchanged. Both reproducibility statements describe the same supplementary ZIP archive and Python notebooks, with identical instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to prior pricing and shape-constrained estimation research are unchanged. Citation reflow in Appendix L does not change the cited literature.

P1.justification: v7 expands the appendix heading and replaces the abbreviated contents outline with a fuller listing of existing subsections and proofs. It also corrects missing words, punctuation, and an index typo in Appendix L's opening paragraph; the main narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix contents becomes a two-page hierarchy with page numbers. Tables 1 and 2, previously on separate pages, appear together on v7 page 15, and early appendix text reflows. Figure designs and table contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The fuller, page-numbered appendix contents makes the lengthy proofs and simulation subsections easier to locate. Grouping Tables 1–2 and correcting Appendix L's prose also improves readability. These are limited usability gains; the scientific arguments and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
